title: Operationalizing the Motivated Intruder: A Codebook-Guided Inference Framework for Semantic Input Privacy in LLMs
abstract: The integration of LLMs into professional and personal workflows creates a semantic leakage vector, where sensitive data is exposed through contextual quasi-identifiers rather than explicit identifiers. We demonstrate that conventional syntactic sanitization (Regex/NER) is fundamentally insufficient for this threat model. To address this, we propose a codebook-guided privacy gateway, an architecture that operationalizes the GDPR's motivated intruder test into executable chain-of-thought logic. We evaluate this framework using a high-fidelity reference model to isolate logical validity from hardware constraints, validating results against a multi-stage human-annotated ground truth ($N=127$) to eliminate model-preference bias. Our findings are threefold. First, deductive inference outperforms pattern matching: the gateway achieves a 90% risk neutralization rate for trade secrets, significantly outperforming baseline methods which neutralize less than 5%. Second, privacy is a compute-bound task: sanitization efficacy correlates linearly ($r=0.985$) with chain-of-thought token volume, mapping a significant inference gap in current local models on consumer-grade hardware. Third, we identify the semantic coupling limit: a structural boundary in technical domains where robust privacy and high utility are mutually exclusive. This study establishes that effective input sanitization requires a shift from deterministic filtering to probabilistic, deductive inference.

title: Consumer Perception and Preferences towards AI Chatbots: An Empirical Study of E-Commerce Users in Ludhiana
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots have become a defining feature of the online shopping experience, reshaping the way e-commerce platforms communicate with and serve their customers. This study examines consumer perception, trust, and attitude toward AI chatbots in the context of online retail, and identifies the key factors that drive their preference and adoption among shoppers. An analytical research design was adopted, with primary data gathered through a structured questionnaire administered to 145 respondents from Ludhiana who had prior experience using AI chatbots while shopping online. Respondents were selected through random sampling, and the resulting data were examined using mean analysis and exploratory factor analysis. The findings indicate that consumers hold a broadly favourable view of AI chatbots, rating them positively for their helpfulness, ease of use, and convenience during the purchase process. Attitudes toward chatbot usage were equally encouraging, pointing to a growing willingness among consumers to rely on AI-driven assistance while shopping online. Trust, while moderately high overall, was tempered by lingering concerns over data privacy, security, and the reliability of chatbot responses. Exploratory factor analysis further revealed three underlying dimensions shaping chatbot adoption: User Acceptance, Perceived Convenience, and Behavioural Intention. Taken together, the results suggest that while AI chatbots are increasingly seen as valuable shopping companions, e-commerce businesses must continue to invest in stronger data security, deeper personalization, and more responsive design if they are to fully earn consumer trust and sustain long-term adoption. Keywords: Consumer Perception, Trust, Attitude, AI Chatbots, Consumer Preferences, Customer Satisfaction, E-commerce

title: Diagnosing AI Transformation in Consulting Engagements: The Balanced Automation Framework
abstract: Consulting engagements for AI-driven transformations frequently fail not because of technology, but because consultants lack a reliable way to diagnose and improve a client's readiness for human-AI collaboration. This paper provides that tool: the Balanced Automation Framework (BAF). The BAF is a deployable diagnostic that changes how AI engagements are run. Instead of relying on generic AI advice, consultants can use the BAF to systematically assess client capabilities, design targeted interventions for competency development, and structure a phased implementation that aligns with the client's specific context. This shifts the engagement from a technology-centric deployment to a capability-building partnership, materially increasing the probability of successful client transformation.

title: Scaling Model Size and Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance in English Intermediate-Task Training
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the scaling of model size affect the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of English intermediate-task training, as measured by F1 scores on the XTREME benchmark? title: Data-Consistency Loop SMOTE: A Closed-Loop Over-sampling Algorithm for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often leading to biased classifiers that perform poorly on the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its blind linear interpolation mechanism frequently introduces noisy samples and causes boundary blurring, failing to preserve the underlying distribution of the original data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Data-Consistency Loop SMOTE (DCL-SMOTE). Unlike traditional unidirectional sampling approaches, DCL-SMOTE establishes a self-adaptive, closed-loop iteration system driven by a "generation -> consistency check -> correction -> re-generation" workflow. The proposed algorithm evaluates each synthetic candidate through multi-dimensional consistency checkers encompassing probability distribution, spatial geometry, and manifold structure. Samples failing the evaluation are dynamically adjusted via gradient-based optimization in the correction module or discarded to trigger a feedback mechanism that adaptively refines the sampling weights of the baseline minority instances. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the closed-loop feedback and self-healing mechanism effectively ensure that the generated samples conform strictly to the authentic minority distribution. This framework provides a robust and mathematically rigorous solution for pattern recognition and classification tasks in high-dimensional imbalanced domains.

title: An Improved SMOTE Oversampling Algorithm Based on a Multi-Strategy Voting Mechanism
abstract: Classifying imbalanced data remains a critical challenge in machine learning, as standard algorithms often favor the majority class and compromise the classification accuracy of the minority class. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this issue by interpolating new samples linearly. However, its uniform generation strategy frequently introduces noisy data and blurs class boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on a multi-strategy voting mechanism, termed Data-voting SMOTE. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on a single geometric model, the proposed method concurrently deploys three distinct generation strategies: standard linear interpolation, Gaussian perturbation center expansion, and three-point recombination centroiding. To ensure the quality of the synthesized data, a multi-indicator evaluation framework is established to quantify the spatial properties of each candidate sample based on density security and distance harmony. A majority voting mechanism then filters these candidates, accepting the final synthetic sample only when a consensus is reached among the strategies. This collaborative approach significantly enhances sample diversity while preserving sharp decision boundaries, thereby effectively reducing noise generation and improving the generalization performance of classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: Rule-chain SMOTE: An Oversampling Method Based on Rule-chain Inference Systems
abstract: Classifying imbalanced datasets remains a critical challenge in machine learning, as traditional classifiers tend to favor the majority class. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) mitigates this by generating synthetic instances through linear numerical interpolation between minority examples. However, this geometric approach often ignores the underlying logical relationships and business rules between features, leading to the creation of unrealistic "ghost samples" and poor handling of mixed-type data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Rule-chain SMOTE, a novel oversampling methodology that replaces traditional numerical interpolation with a logical rule-chain inference system. Instead of filling space blindly, the proposed method treats sample generation as a chain-deduction process. By selecting and slightly perturbing core root features from real minority samples, the algorithm triggers a sequence of interconnected deterministic or probabilistic rules to sequentially deduce and complete the remaining features. This topological inference mechanism ensures that the generated samples strictly adhere to the intrinsic causal relationships and manifold constraints of the data. Rule-chain SMOTE naturally accommodates mixed-type features without losing statistical meaning through forced continuous encoding. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the method significantly improves the logical soundness and interpretability of synthetic data while effectively preserving class boundaries, offering a robust and explainable framework for imbalanced learning.

title: A Contrastive Boundary Push SMOTE Over-sampling Algorithm for Imbalanced Data Learning
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, where classifiers often bias toward the majority class due to the skewed distribution of data. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this by interpolating synthetic instances within the minority class space. However, traditional SMOTE frequently generates samples that invade the majority class region, leading to severe class-overlapping and blurred decision boundaries. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling method named Contrastive Boundary Push SMOTE (CBP-SMOTE). The core idea of CBP-SMOTE is to explicitly integrate the philosophy of contrastive learning into the data generation process. Specifically, after synthesizing a baseline instance, the algorithm identifies its nearest neighbor in the majority (negative) class space and constructs a push vector. By leveraging a distance-based feedback mechanism, the baseline instance is explicitly pushed away from the negative class representation space. This mechanism effectively sharpens the decision boundary and suppresses the overlapping effect. Theoretical and procedural analyses demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly clarifies class boundaries while maintaining the diversity of the minority class, thereby enhancing the generalization performance of classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: Multi-View SMOTE: Separate Generation and Alignment for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Multi-View Learning
abstract: Multi-view learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm in machine learning, where objects are characterized by multiple heterogeneous feature subsets or data sources. However, the ubiquitous class imbalance problem significantly undermines the classification performance in real-world multi-view applications. Traditional synthetic minority over-sampling techniques (SMOTE) are primarily designed for single-view data and fail to handle the complex structural correlations across different views. Directly applying single-view SMOTE to each view independently disrupts the alignment and cross-view consistency of the synthesized data, while feature concatenation severely exacerbates the curse of dimensionality. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Multi-view SMOTE. The proposed algorithm decomposes the multi-view over-sampling process into a separate generation stage and a joint alignment stage. In the first stage, raw synthetic minority samples are independently generated within each distinct feature space using localized topological interpolation, preserving the specific characteristics of each individual view. In the second stage, a multi-view alignment mechanism is established by mapping all views into a unified lower-dimensional latent subspace. Cross-view consistency is enforced by minimizing the discrepancy among the projected representations of the minority class. A consensus representation is subsequently synthesized in the latent space and back-projected to the original view-specific spaces via pseudo-inverse reconstruction, ensuring that the final synthetic samples are perfectly aligned across all views. Theoretical formulations validate that Multi-view SMOTE effectively prevents semantic misalignment while mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The proposed framework provides an efficient, robust, and highly interpretable data-augmentation solution for imbalanced multi-view classification tasks.

title: МЕТОДИ ПІДВИЩЕННЯ ТОЧНОСТІ КЛАСИФІКАЦІЇ ДАНИХ НА ОСНОВІ АНСАМБЛЕВИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ МАШИННОГО НАВЧАННЯ
abstract: МЕТОДИ ПІДВИЩЕННЯ ТОЧНОСТІ КЛАСИФІКАЦІЇ ДАНИХ НА ОСНОВІ АНСАМБЛЕВИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ МАШИННОГО НАВЧАННЯ Анотація.У статті досліджено методи підвищення точності класифікації даних на основі використання ансамблевих моделей машинного навчання в умовах оброблення багатовимірних та різнорідних інформаційних вибірок.Актуальність дослідження зумовлена необхідністю підвищення ефективності функціонування інтелектуальних інформаційних систем аналізу даних у задачах підтримки прийняття рішень, що застосовуються у сфері кібербезпеки, медичної діагностики, економічного прогнозування, технічного моніторингу та інших прикладних галузях.Зростання обсягів структурованих і неструктурованих даних, наявність шумів у вибірках та складність нелінійних залежностей між ознаками обумовлюють потребу у використанні сучасних методів підвищення точності класифікації на основі інтеграції результатів роботи декількох базових алгоритмів машинного навчання.У роботі запропоновано підхід до побудови stacking-ансамблю, який забезпечує інтеграцію результатів роботи моделей Random Forest, Gradient Boosting та багатошарової нейронної мережі з використанням метакласифікатора узагальнення результатів прогнозування.Проведено експериментальне дослідження ефективності запропонованого підходу на еталонному наборі даних Breast Cancer Wisconsin Dataset із використанням процедури кросвалідації та стандартних метрик оцінювання якості класифікації, зокрема точності класифікації, precision, recall та F1-міри.Отримані результати експерименту показали підвищення точності класифікації ансамблевої моделі у межах від 0,8% до 3,1% порівняно з окремими базовими алгоритмами машинного навчання, що підтверджує ефективність застосування stackingпідходу для задач класифікації багатовимірних даних.Наукова новизна отриманих результатів полягає у розробленні підходу до інтеграції моделей різної алгоритмічної природи у складі stacking-ансамблю для підвищення точності класифікації даних шляхом зменшення дисперсії прогнозу, систематичної похибки та ризику перенавчання моделі.

title: CA-LIME: A Collinearity-Aware LIME Framework for Reliable and Interpretable Explanations in Healthcare AI
abstract: In clinical tabular models, correlated biomarkers can make local explanations unstable even when predictive performance appears acceptable. This paper presents CA-LIME, a collinearity-aware extension of LIME built to address that failure mode directly. Five variations of CA-LIME Vanilla reference, VIF, PCA back projection, Ridge, and ElasticNet allow us to investigate how various correlation-control strategies alter explanation behavior. ILPD, Kaggle liver, a combined ILPD + Kaggle liver cohort, and heart stroke are the four dataset configurations on which we test the system. Existing validated ILPD/stroke assets are reused, and the same workflow is extended to the new liver parameters for consistency. With an emphasis on local interpretability, stability, clinical plausibility, and practical application, we also contrast CA-LIME with SHAP as the baseline explanation. Across settings, CA-LIME retains clinically meaningful feature emphasis and shows stable local behavior under correlated inputs. The findings clarify the remaining validation and deployment constraints while supporting CA-LIME as a decision-support explanation layer.

title: HOW ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CAN TRANSFORM BUSINESS DECISION-MAKING AND STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT FOR AGRIBUSINESSES
abstract: In today's environment, artificial intelligence (AI), a set of technologies that mimic individual aspects of human thinking and behavior, is evolving into a powerful tool for supporting corporate management decisions. It enables companies to assess not only their current status but also formulate long-term strategies based on predictive models. Using the example of Agrofirm Svoboda CJSC, we propose a comprehensive model for using AI to improve the validity of management decisions, forecast key financial indicators, manage risks, conduct strategic planning and scenario modeling, and generate reports, forecasts, and possible scenarios online, facilitating the work of specialists. Overall, this article examines the importance of AI in improving the efficiency of agricultural production and proposes promising areas for its development, combining the latest technologies with the current conditions and needs of agricultural producers. This will enable Agrofirm Svoboda CJSC to apply innovative management approaches, making the company a leader in its industry, and AI will become a key data provider for strategic decisions.

title: Computational Complexity in Timed Argumentation Frameworks
abstract: Timed Argumentation Frameworks (TAFs) allow taking into account the availability of arguments and attacks in abstract argumentation. We propose a new reasoning approach for TAFs, where a standard Dung-style AF can be associated with each timepoint. We show that, although this framework is more expressive than Dung's framework, our approach does not lead to an increase in computational complexity for most reasoning problems and classical extension-based semantics.

title: Models of Legal Protection for Works Created with Involvement of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The research focuses on the legal mechanisms for protecting works created using artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, taking into account their creation specifics and the degree of human creative involvement. The subject of the study is the system of legal mechanisms for protecting such works considering their creation features. The aim of the study is to develop theoretical and methodological foundations for a differentiated approach to legal protection of creative works created using AI technologies, and to formulate proposals for improving legislation in this area. The study hypothesizes the need to abandon the binary model of legal regulation (“protected or not protected”) in favor of a differentiated approach to determining the scope of protection depending on the degree of human creative participation and the level of AI system autonomy. The authors methodology includes formal legal, comparative legal, system-structural methods, and legal modeling. Based on the analysis of Russian and foreign legislation, doctrinal approaches, and judicial practice, the research justifies classifying AI works into three categories: those with predominant human creative contribution, hybrid works, and those with minimal human creative input. The study develops a system of criteria for evaluating the originality of algorithmically generated works (statistical uniqueness, result unpredictability, semantic coherence, aesthetic/functional value). A three-tier model of legal regulation for using protected works in machine learning processes is promoted, along with specific proposals for improving Russian intellectual property legislation considering modern technological challenges: amendments to Article 1228 of the Civil Code regarding criteria for the creative nature of an author’s activity when using AI; to Article 1259 — on the specifics of AI works’ legal regime; to Article 1274 — on free use of works for machine learning purposes; to Article 1286 — on licensing peculiarities for using works in machine learning; and introducing a new paragraph to Chapter 71 of the Code regulating rights to works created with minimal human creative participation (15-year protection period, indication of AI application).

abstract: The imagination is the powerhouse of the mind. title: Improving Cypher Query Generation from Natural Language using Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
abstract: This study addresses the automated generation of Cypher queries from natural language expressions for graph databases, systematically analyzing the impact of various training strategies and data augmentation techniques on model performance. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential in natural language-to-query tasks, their generalization to unseen schemas and structural accuracy remain critical challenges. In this context, the study investigates the contributions of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and cross-domain training strategies utilizing relational database (SQL) data to the Text-to-Cypher task.

title: Enhanced Transformer Powered Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Contrastive Embedding and Unified Discrimination
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced Anomaly Transformer for unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series. We introduce a contrastive embedding module that refines the input embedding by optimizing a lightweight MLP with an InfoNCE objective, where positive pairs are pulled closer while negative pairs are pushed apart in the feature space. We further propose Unified Discrimination at the decision stage, which unifies reconstruction error and association discrepancy into a single anomaly score. Experiments on four large-scale benchmarks (SMD, PSM, MSL, and SMAP) demonstrate consistent performance gains over the Anomaly Transformer baseline, improving Precision and F1-score while maintaining high Recall, with an average F1-score of 0.9554.

title: A Lyapunov-Guided Post-Action Shield for Stability-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a Lyapunov-guided post-action shielding mechanism for deep reinforcement learning (DRL) controllers under bounded actuation disturbances. In addition, an energy-safety requirement is formulated as a one-step energy threshold constraint that keeps the predicted next-state energy proxy within a prescribed limit, using a bounded-disturbance worst-case check. Simulation results show that the proposed mechanism substantially reduces constraint violations under actuation noise while preserving the nominal policy behavior whenever possible.

title: Physics-Informed Imitation Learning for Resilient Autonomous Driving
abstract: Imitation learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for autonomous vehicle control. However, existing policies often suffer from severe covariate shift and lack explicit stability guarantees in closed-loop trajectory tracking. This paper proposes an adaptive Lyapunov-constrained imitation learning framework for vehicle trajectory tracking. To address the covariate shift problem, we explicitly embed a discrete-time kinematic bicycle model into the policy training process. This differentiable physical prior enables propagation of the nominal tracking error and allows a global Lyapunov decay constraint to be directly employed on the policy optimization via an Actor-Critic architecture. To prevent the overly aggressive penalization near the reference trajectory, we introduce a state-dependent adaptive decay rate that relaxes the constraint for small errors while strengthening it under large deviations. As a result, the proposed method achieves both high tracking precision and strong recovery from model uncertainties and disturbances. Extensive experiments in interactive traffic environments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in collision avoidance and disturbance rejection.
